name: Grounded goal agent: the engine that answers and works on a person's goals from their own material, and the executor that runs their queued AI tasks
description: The one engine that takes a person's goal from question to finished work: it answers from their own material, carries out what they ask, and runs their queued tasks, configured per consumer rather than rebuilt for each.
purpose: Keeps a person's or team's goals moving by answering from their own material, carrying out requested changes, and running queued work to a written standard.
approach: Grounds each answer and action in the person's own goals and material, and reports every task result against the goal it serves.
out_of_scope: Rendering a chat interface, storing goal data, holding any one organization's names, rules or data, running as a hosted service, and taking decisions that belong to a person.
milestones: 1. Queued tasks meet their written goal without human rework, at a cost per task the operator accepts. 2. Realistic chat turns pass their rubric on grounded facts, right handling and exact changes, at a cost per passing turn the operator accepts. 3. No unrequested write is made, no requested write is missing, and no human-only step is taken without a person. 4. No item from another user, team or quest reaches a prompt or store. 5. Every solution has a current measured result, and its selection follows that result. 6. Each consumer writes no glue of its own and copies no engine code into itself.
knowledge: Agent loop research (reason and act, plan and execute, verification against a written goal); retrieval-augmented generation and context selection; evaluation of language-model systems; Quest's model of quests, goals, notes, asks and AI tasks; the operating principle "AI acts first, humans confirm"; Joshua's evolvable structure that optimizes intent.
measures_of_success: People's goals move through delegated work; tasks and replies need no correction; operators accept the cost; Joshua can steer by reviewing metrics without needing to read code. Standing conditions: Chat turns that pass their rubric (grounded facts, right handling, exact changes) at a cost per passing turn the operator accepts; queued tasks that meet their written goal; no unrequested writes and no human-only step taken alone; no data across scope; every part measured and selected by its metric.
parameters: One configuration per lane: the consumer's adapters (retrieval, cards, conversations, escalation, deep runner), model tiers and providers, personas, budgets and schedules, and the implementation selected for each swappable solution.
inputs: A person's message or a queued task, the quest and goal it concerns, and the sources the adapters reach.
outputs: A reply, a task result reported against its goal, a decision-request for a person, or files and records changed as requested.
effects: Writes to Quest and other systems through their APIs and tools; model and search spend; context cards and conversation memory kept for later turns.
usage_notes: Two entry points share one brain: the importable core (`Orchestrator`) for chat and other hosts, and the runner (a lane that polls, claims, runs, escalates and reports) for queued work. A terminal chat drives the same brain. Every specific comes through configuration; nothing about a consumer is built in.

name: Tiered model provider layer
description: One calling surface over several model vendors, so adding, dropping or switching a vendor is a configuration change and no caller has to know which vendor serves a model.
purpose: Send each planning and answering call to the vendor that serves its model name, so AI work for people keeps moving when one vendor fails or runs out of quota.
approach: Send each model call to the vendor that serves its name, and recover from transient failures and exhausted quota by retrying or stepping down a tier.
out_of_scope: Deciding which tier a piece of work needs, and writing the content of a prompt.
milestones: 1. Offline routing, tier fallback, retry and cost cases passed by the multi provider: 56 of 56, with each model name served by its own vendor. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. Live pass rate and latency per model tier recorded on the same cases, so the cheapest passing tier is known rather than assumed.
knowledge: Models route by name prefix to their vendor; a vendor with no key is simply not registered. Transient errors deserve bounded retries while quota errors deserve a lower tier, and a give-up records a process-wide outage. Price tables count input tokens only, and no live latency or pass rate per tier has been recorded. Keyless subscription-based execution through a local command-line tool is an option where no API key exists.
measures_of_success: The right provider serves each model name, a quota error falls to a working tier, transient errors are retried the right number of times, and cost estimates order tiers correctly, all on offline cases.
parameters: Model backend selection, per-tier model pins, vendor keys and base addresses, retry count and base delay, and the registry that maps tiers to model identifiers.
inputs: A planning request (prompt plus a forced tool schema) or an answering request (messages plus an optional system prompt), with a model name or tier and optional step and reasoning hints.
outputs: A raw decision dictionary for planning, answer text for answering, and a live list of available model identifiers; errors are formatted for humans.
effects: Network calls to model vendors (or a spawned local command-line process), spend, and a process-wide outage marker after a give-up.
usage_notes: Wrap vendors in the multi-provider and let the registry resolve tiers. Prefer the cheapest tier that passes the task's own evaluation, and pin a vendor only deliberately.

name: Live messaging channel transport
description: A two-way link to a live chat channel that keeps messages in order and survives malformed events and gateway failures without ending the conversation.
purpose: Receive and send messages on a live external chat channel, so each message in a conversation with a person arrives once and in order.
approach: Pass each inbound and outbound message through the channel gateway once and in order, and skip events that carry no readable message.
out_of_scope: Operating the gateway itself, and approving permissions on its behalf.
milestones: 1. Offline channel cases passed by the OpenClaw bridge: 20 of 20, covering ordered inbound messages, malformed events and dead gateways. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. Channel cases passed on a live OpenClaw gateway, once its wire shapes are confirmed against it.
knowledge: The gateway's wire shapes were written from documentation without a live gateway, so the evidence is conformance to tolerant guesses. The gateway has had a serious authentication-token vulnerability, so the bridge requires a patched version, disabled skills and plugins, and never approves permissions itself. Approvals belong to the host's decision flow.
measures_of_success: Offline cases pass: ordered inbound messages, spelling drift in keys, ignored non-message and malformed events, graceful wire failure and dead gateway, long-poll clamp, attachments, correct send arguments and ids, only allowed tools called, and idempotent close. Standing conditions: Deliver every message exactly once and in order, survive malformed events and gateway failure without raising, and restrict calls to the allowed tool set.
parameters: Token file, channel name, whether to fetch attachments, and the receive timeout in seconds.
inputs: For receive, a timeout; for send, an outbound reply with chat reference, text and optional reply-to id.
outputs: An inbound batch (messages with ids, chat references, text and attachments, a healthy flag and any error) and a send result with success and message id.
effects: Network calls to the gateway for long-poll, send and attachment fetch; close tears down the held connection. Every failure is returned as a value, never raised.
usage_notes: Run the gateway locked down as documented, call receive in a loop, treat an empty batch as normal, and add a channel through gateway configuration or a second transport implementing the protocol.

name: Overseer: risk management that raises the overall metric
description: Watches every run through cheap checks and acts only on high-risk cases; for each kind of risk it applies whatever response the metrics show addresses that risk best (a model tier, a narrow question, a rule, a hand-off), chosen per category with statistical significance, so risk is handled where it is and paid for only there.
purpose: Raises the AI's overall evaluation metric by handling each high-risk case with the response proven best for its risk.
approach: Detects high-risk cases with cheap checks and answers each risk category with the response its metric shows works best, with statistical significance against no response.
out_of_scope: Reviewing low-risk cases, which proceed untouched, and reading the full body of each operation where a compact digest is enough.
milestones: 1. Each risk category the overseer handles has a cheap detector and a labelled case set, and overseer and no_overseer have recorded results per category. 2. For each category, the selected response beats no response on that category's cases with statistical significance, at a cost the overall metric accepts. 3. The overall QAR metric is higher with the overseer on than off.
knowledge: The digest must show the evidence each label depends on, shedding old history operations first and prior escalations last so the refusal rule keeps its evidence. A failure must degrade to proceed, and a degraded flag lets a caller retry at another tier so a silent overseer is distinguishable from a healthy one. Human escalation is for genuine forks only, since routine work is AI-doable. Checked in the code on 2026-10-28: the overseer is on by default, at the quality tier in the library and at the balanced tier in the Quest host, capped per run (core/orchestrator_types.py); an older note that it is off by default is wrong. Open, for the specification owner to decide: the recommendation is to keep it as its own solution, because it watches one run from a digest, while a hint learned from past outcomes is intuition, which the owner places in the subconscious (remember-and-recall, outcome_precedents). On cheap-model routing a reviewer handed a decision scored worse than no review while the same model asked one question of fact did well, so fact_questions is the alternative to try and no_overseer is a real rival, not a floor. The other options are merging it with a learned hint into one solution, dissolving it into the working stream or the long view, or renaming it; none is decided. Unconfirmed: these two alternatives are proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm. The specification owner's definition (2026-10-28): the overseer is responsible for risk management to improve the overall evaluation metric; it is called when cheap checks notice high-risk cases and does whatever addresses that risk category well according to metrics with statistical significance for each risk, whether a particular model tier or anything else, flexible to each type. This settles the earlier open question of keeping it. An earlier labelled run in July passed every digest on a model since replaced, but it is not in the results log; the overseer was switched on by default then.
measures_of_success: Per risk category, the chosen response beats no response with statistical significance; low-risk cases pay no review cost; the overall evaluation metric rises. Standing conditions: A failed response degrades to proceed and never blocks a run. Never decide from keywords in a model's own output.
parameters: The risk categories, each one's cheap detector and threshold, the response chosen per category (tier, question, rule or hand-off), the significance level, and the per-run cap.
inputs: A digest string built from the user message, goal, step counters, the plan, recent conversation, prior escalations and recent operation summaries.
outputs: For a flagged case: the risk category, the response applied and its signal (proceed, redirect with a hint, answer now, escalate to deep execution, escalate to a person), with a reason and a degraded flag.
effects: Cheap checks on every run; a response, possibly a model call, only on flagged cases; no other writes; never raises.
usage_notes: Selected today: the digest overseer, one prompt for every risk, after a free pre-filter. The proposal is per_risk_response.

name: Queued-task runner lane
description: A queued task runs once, under the persona it names, and always comes back with a reported result, including after a restart.
purpose: Takes a person's queued requests to a reported outcome, so they run on time without anyone having to start them by hand.
approach: Claims each due task once, runs it, and reports the result back to its queue.
out_of_scope: Deciding what a queued task should say or do.
milestones: 1. Every lifecycle case passes on the lane's poller and executor: done, failed, needs-you, duplicate, lost claim, not-yet-due, team-scoped and unconfigured. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: Discovery is event driven with signature dedup across restarts and a backend-aware claim as a second guard. A persona activates only when asked for, never from a bare mention of a name. Folder sync keeps human text and pushes each bullet once. Cancelled tasks need no patch because the backend already set the status.
measures_of_success: Poll, claim, run and report behave correctly across done, failed, needs-you, duplicate, lost-claim, not-yet-due, team-scoped and unconfigured cases, with persona choice, folder sync and scheduling correct. Standing conditions: Claim each due task once. Run it as the right persona against its work folder. Report an outcome for every task. Run none early.
parameters: The poller takes a configuration with credentials, team, adapters and a concurrency bound; personas take a skills root, registry, assignment fields and flags for model-judged asks; the lane driver takes check, once or loop modes and an env file.
inputs: Queued tasks from the backend, the configuration, persona registry and folder map.
outputs: A reported status on each task (with result text or decision id), updated folder sync files, and logs.
effects: Claims tasks on the backend, writes the sync file in work folders, may post notes, and spawns deep runs.
usage_notes: Start a lane with the shared driver and pick one-shot mode for cron or loop mode for a service. Use structured assignment for personas where tasks name an owner.

name: Cost estimation, daily budget and host load guard
description: Stops a lane's spending at a daily token budget and pauses task pickup under host overload, without ever killing work already running.
purpose: Keeps a lane's spending and host load predictable, so a runaway day cannot drain the budget or overload the machine.
approach: Estimates what each operation will cost and holds back new work once a daily budget or host limit is reached.
out_of_scope: Real provider invoices, output-token billing, and work run on a subscription-based runner, which the daily budget does not count.
milestones: 1. Prices, cost estimates, the daily total across restarts, and the pause-and-resume guard for memory, free memory and load pass every offline case. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: Shallow orchestrator calls can run away on cost, so a daily cap is opt-in and persisted. Pausing pickup is lossless because unclaimed tasks stay queued and fire on a later scan. Prices are a hand-kept snapshot of list prices, so a provider change is not noticed until the table is edited.
measures_of_success: Prices and estimates are arithmetically right, the daily total survives a restart and resets each day, bad or negative values are handled, and the guard pauses and resumes without flapping.
parameters: Provider and model names, a token count, daily limit and usage path from the environment, and optional host limits for memory percent, free memory and load.
inputs: Token counts per call, environment variables, and host samples of memory and load.
outputs: A price per million input tokens, a bootstrap cost estimate with the provider and model used, a running total with an over-limit flag and status line, and a paused or not verdict.
effects: Writes the day's tally to a usage file and signals the poller to stop picking up new tasks while over budget or overloaded; in-flight tasks are never killed.
usage_notes: Both limits are opt-in; set them per lane. Review the price table whenever a provider changes prices.

name: Evolve by metric
description: Keeps every part of QAR comparable by its metric, so a better model, method or tool replaces the current one by measurement instead of by rewrite. It also connects QAR to a tool, search engine, model vendor, agent or knowledge source through an open-source hub and the standard it speaks, so a new capability arrives by configuration and no code per integration; how far that holds is scored by score-hub-connections of the hub of hubs, over the hub registry.
purpose: Keep every part of QAR specified as a solution with alternatives, a metric and a selected implementation, so the best one is used as the state of the art moves.
approach: Select each part's implementation by its recorded measurement, and replace it when a rival measures better on the same cases.
out_of_scope: It avoids saying what QAR is for: that is the top intent, and the general machinery for checking, measuring and selecting is the evolvable-structure library's.
milestones: 1. Share of QAR solutions whose selected implementation has a recorded result on committed code and is not beaten by a rival on the same cases: 100%.
knowledge: The author's evolvable structure (intents, problems, solutions, implementations, ideals and metrics); the evolvable-structure library's checks, measurement harness and selector.
measures_of_success: Every solution has a recorded result on committed code, selections follow the measurements, and Joshua can steer by reviewing metrics without reading code. Standing conditions: Every part of QAR has a record, a current measured result and a selection that follows the measurement; a better model, method or tool replaces the current one without a rewrite.
parameters: The records under esoi, the esoi configuration, the evaluation components.
inputs: A change to the code, a new alternative, or a new model or tool to compare.
outputs: Checked records, recorded metric results and the selected implementation for each solution.
effects: Result rows are appended to the evaluation log; no model spend unless a paid arm is run by decision.
usage_notes: Run esoi check before committing and esoi run --stale after committing measured code. Paid arms follow the metric run policy.

name: Mind: one goal-focused working stream per request
description: Gives every step of a request the same running account of it (what the person asked, what it was resolved to mean, what was refused or corrected, what earlier steps found), carried from step to step instead of rebuilt, so a fast-tier model acts with a continuity one prompt per step cannot give it.
purpose: Keeps every step of a person's request acting on everything the request has established so far, at the cost of the fast tier.
approach: Carries one working stream per request from its first step to its answer, adds only what the admission gate lets in, and reuses the cached part instead of re-sending it.
out_of_scope: What carries across requests and sessions, and deciding which items are worth adding: the stream holds what it is given.
milestones: 1. A labelled set of multi-step requests exists in which a later step needs something established earlier (a refusal, a correction, the resolved request, an earlier finding), and rebuilt_per_step has a recorded result on it. 2. A carried stream scores at or above rebuilt_per_step on that set with the chat judge pass rate held and input cost per request no higher than rebuilt_full_context.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm. The specification owner's design: a stream of consciousness focused only on the goal condition of this request, seeing only what relates to it, on the fast tier, because a coding agent is reliable through one long cached session. Read in the code on 2026-10-28, not yet reproduced on a live turn: each planner step is one fresh call (core/orchestrator_planning.py); a cached prefix of head and context layers spans the calls of a turn (core/prompt_layers.py); from the second step the transcript and the context block are swapped for a note saying they were given at step one (core/orchestrator_events.py, on by default in core/orchestrator_constants.py), and that block is where the resolved request, declined proposals, guidance, recent context and cards are prepended (core/orchestrator_run_begin.py); older observations collapse to one line past a recency window (core/planner_context.py). Swapping the context layer also changes the cached prefix, so later steps give up a cheap cache read of the context rather than a full-price one. The final answer still gets the full context. Deep work already runs as one continued session through the deep runner, so this solution concerns the in-process planning loop. From a founder's team meeting on 2026-10-27: the chat is weaker than a task sent to a coding agent because the library is a partial harness; the owner named three directions (near-perfect routing so hard requests reach a deep run, stored context so simple ones need none, or adopting an open-source harness, which the owner placed in the world, as an option to replace the coding agent for doing things: claim-reach), and wants high quality from a low-tier model through the structure of prompts and code, with the high tier kept for what matters most, such as plan generation.
measures_of_success: On multi-step requests no later step contradicts, re-proposes or ignores what an earlier step or the person established; the chat judge pass rate holds; input cost per request stays within that of re-sending the context from cache. Standing conditions: Never tell a model it saw something it was not given. Keep the stream inside the request's scope.
parameters: The implementation, the model tier, the stream's token budget and compaction point, and whether the context layer is re-sent, referenced or carried.
inputs: The person's message, the transcript, the resolved request and goal condition, the admitted context and each step's admitted observations.
outputs: Each step's view of the request (a carried message list or a rebuilt prompt), with the step's decision added to it.
effects: Planner-tier model calls; a provider prompt cache is written and read. No store writes.
usage_notes: Selected today: rebuilt_per_step. Compare rebuilt_full_context first, since it is one existing configuration flag, then a carried stream. Decision teamdec_a658ad84e023 (hold, no build).

name: Subconscious: the person's own knowledge, admitted to the working stream by the goal
description: Draws on what the person's own material holds (their cards, files, notes, past conversations and recalled context) and decides at every step what of it enters the working stream, by whether it bears on the request's goal condition, with the scope fence applied once at that gate.
purpose: Keeps each request's working stream holding the part of the person's own knowledge its goal needs, so a fast model is neither misled by near misses nor buried in noise.
approach: Judges each candidate from the person's material against the request's goal condition and scope before it enters the working stream, settling clear cases cheaply and asking a small model only on the borderline.
out_of_scope: Finding the candidates (retrieval, card selection and reading keep their own specifications), and knowledge about the world beyond the person's own material.
milestones: 1. A labelled set of steps exists, each with candidate items marked needed, irrelevant, near miss or out of scope, and recency_window has a recorded result on it. 2. A goal-conditioned implementation admits more needed items than recency_window at the same or better precision, with no out-of-scope item admitted.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm. The specification owner's design: the subconscious is the person's own knowledge and context; it does context assembly and tool calls and checks which context is worth showing to the mind. Assembly and reading are already specified (select-context, gather-evidence, search-cards-and-specs, recall-recent-context); this solution adds only the admission check, which no existing record owns. Today cards are filtered once at the start (core/card_filter.py) and observations are admitted by recency (core/planner_context.py). Its value grows with a carried stream, where an admitted item stays for every later step. On cheap-model routing a reviewer handed a decision argued with correct decisions while the same model asked one question of fact did well, so the borderline judge asks whether an item bears on the goal, never whether the plan is right. The specification owner's direction (2026-10-28): intuition is conceptually part of the subconscious. Recorded as outcome_precedents: at admission, past requests like this one and how they ended are surfaced to the working stream as a hint, never as a decision; the outcome history is kept by the long view (hold-the-intents). The anticipation engine predicts the next ask and recipes replay past successes; neither learns from how a turn ended, so this is new.
measures_of_success: Needed items are admitted, irrelevant and near-miss items are kept out, and no out-of-scope item is ever admitted, at no more than one small model call per step. Standing conditions: Apply the scope fence at the gate on every path. Treat an empty or near-miss lookup as not found.
parameters: Thresholds per source, the borderline band that calls the judge, the judge's tier, and the per-step token budget.
inputs: The goal condition, the turn's scope tags, and candidate items with their source and scores.
outputs: The admitted items with a one-line reason each, and the dropped ones with theirs, for the explanation of how an answer was reached.
effects: At most one small model call per step for borderline items; no writes.
usage_notes: Sits between retrieval and the working stream. Selected today: recency_window.

name: Science: evidence-weighted knowledge about the world
description: Answers what a request needs to know about the world beyond the person's own material from evidence sources (a host's research and experience search interfaces first, the web after), and says for each claim where it came from and how strong its evidence is.
purpose: Gives people advice and facts about the world they can weigh, from the best evidence the host can reach.
approach: Consults the strongest available evidence source for a world question before the cheapest, and carries each claim's source and evidence strength into the working stream.
out_of_scope: The person's own material, acting in the world, and deciding which question to research next on the person's behalf.
milestones: 1. A labelled set of world questions exists, each with reference sources and the strength of their evidence, and web_with_support_check has a recorded result on it. 2. research_sources_first cites a supporting source for more claims than web_with_support_check on that set, with stated confidence that matches how often the claims hold, at a cost per answer within the chat budget.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm. The specification owner's design: a solution for science that represents world knowledge, using existing interfaces for research and experience search, related to web search. Web research is already specified (search-the-web) and stays the open-web reader this solution calls; the library has no research-source adapter yet, so a host's research or experience search reaches a run today only as a retrieval source or a custom tool. The answer check already flags claims the turn's reads do not support and rewrites them once with their basis (core/orchestrator_judges.py).
measures_of_success: World claims cite a source that supports them; stated confidence matches how often such claims hold; a host's research sources are used when they cover the question; the chat and background work give the same answer from the same evidence. Standing conditions: Keep world knowledge apart from the person's own material. Never present general knowledge as a cited finding.
parameters: The research sources a host declares and their order, the web reader, the evidence labels, and the cost cap per answer.
inputs: A world question from the request and the host's declared research sources.
outputs: Findings, each with its source, an evidence-strength label and the passage that supports it.
effects: Calls to research sources and the web within a spending cap; no writes.

name: Body: the host's data model as the agent's own consistent state
description: Treats the host application's own data (in Quest, the person's quests, goals, tasks and decisions) as the agent's body: one current view every step reads to know its own state, changed only through the host's declared operations and read back after every change, so what the AI says about the account is true when it says it. It also knows what the app can do and how it is used, from the host's operations and documentation.
purpose: Lets a person trust what the AI says about their own account and about what it changed in it.
approach: Reads the person's state from the host through one view, changes it only through the host's operations, and re-reads what a change touched before anything is said about it.
out_of_scope: Choosing and carrying out the change a request asks for, which the quest change executor does, and anything outside the host's own data.
milestones: 1. A labelled set of scripted sessions on a disposable account exists, each asking about state before and after changes, and card_and_reads has a recorded result on it. 2. No state claim contradicts the store at reply time, and no change is repeated or re-proposed after it ran, on that set.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm. The specification owner's framing: for the person, the host's database is the body (its structure, its motions, the being that acts), and the AI represents that body when it acts in the world. The owner corrected an earlier view that the body was only a role tag over the operation tools: it needs its own specification. The library stays domain-free: the body is reached through the host's read adapter and tool catalog, and Quest is the first host. A turn is already grounded in a quest through the quest's managed card, rebuilt on sync (runner/quest_folder_index.py); nothing re-reads a quest after the AI changes it.
measures_of_success: Every state claim matches the store when the reply is sent; answers about state agree across a session; a change that ran is reported once and never proposed again; an empty or near-miss lookup never becomes a write. Standing conditions: Change the host's data only through its declared operations. Keep each person's state in their own scope.
parameters: Which objects are read back after a change, how long a read stays current in a session, and the host's read adapter and tool catalog.
inputs: The host's read adapter, the operations the host declares, and each operation's result.
outputs: A current state view for the request's scope with the time each part was read, and after a change the read-back objects.
effects: Reads from the host; writes only through the host's operations.
usage_notes: Selected today: card_and_reads. The change executor stays the motor; this is the body's sense of itself.

name: Higher mind: an AI representative's standing view across its assigned quests, placed in the intent hierarchy
description: Keeps, for each AI representative, one maintained high-level view across the set of quests assigned to it (what was decided, declined, learned and corrected there, and where the work is heading), anchored at the intent those quests serve and reading that intent's ancestors, so a request handled by the representative starts from the broad context of all its quests; a single quest's view is the narrow case. The view reaches only the representative's assigned quests and their ancestor intents, never other representatives' or people's.
purpose: Gives each AI representative a broad, high-level context across the quests it is assigned, so every request it handles starts from what that whole set and its intents have already settled.
approach: Maintains one standing view per representative across its assigned quests, anchored at the intent those quests serve, and hands each request the parts that bear on it, fenced to that representative's quests and their ancestors.
out_of_scope: Continuity within one request; the person's own reflections, intents and specification text, which are read and never rewritten; and creating or linking intents, which only a person does (the AI may ask).
milestones: 1. A labelled set of multi-session cases exists for representatives with several assigned quests under a nested intent hierarchy (a decline on one assigned quest then a related request on another, a correction applied later, chat then background work, a quest assigned to another representative, another person's intent), and separate_stores has a recorded result on it. 2. per_rep_assigned_view passes more of those cases than separate_stores, with no item reaching another representative's quests, a sibling intent or another person, and no time added before the reply.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm. The specification owner's correction (2026-10-28): the higher mind is not per quest; each AI representative has its own higher mind, and every higher mind is associated with an intent, which is itself an ESOI specification. Intents nest recursively: a sub-intent arises as an implementation of a solution in its parent (life intents, then an organisation, then a product, then quests), a quest can sit under an intent at any level, and the depth differs by person and product; the host has backend support for this but no presentation of the hierarchy yet, and the owner asked to leverage it. What the host already has (read in its code 2026-10-28): intents owned by a person, a team or an organisation; one parent link per intent, active only while both sides state it; quest placements under an intent; an intent frame built by code for quest-scoped prompts that names the quest's intent and the level below it, not its ancestors; and a rule that a linked neighbour intent is shown only as far as its owner revealed. What the library has: the intent frame and lazily built quest specification (ground-in-intent), selection of the specification records a request concerns (spec-selection), conversation recall, feedback guidance, the scoped recent-context store, and per-representative learned notes and context preferences (select-context:rep), which carry no quest or intent scope; the scope tag fence compares flat tag sets and has no notion of ancestors. Missing: no view is kept per intent or per representative and intent; nothing walks the hierarchy upward for a request; the fence cannot express visible-to-descendants. The owner's further clarification (2026-10-28): the point of the higher mind is AI representatives with specifically assigned quests, so a representative holds a broader context at a high level across them; the representative and its assigned quests are the primary unit, associated with an intent in the hierarchy, and a single quest's view is the narrow case. How the host assigns them today (read in its code 2026-10-28): a quest lists its assigned representatives, each with the role the person gave it there; every autopilot persona on a quest is also assigned; a reverse lookup and an endpoint list a representative's quests; a goal can name the representative handling it; a representative registry holds its persona, home team and learned notes, which are kept for the representative as a whole. What is missing: no view spans a representative's assigned quests; its learned notes and context preferences are not tied to those quests or their intents; nothing derives the intent the assigned quests serve; and the fence cannot say a representative's own quests and their ancestors. Open recommendation: per_rep_assigned_view, since it is the owner's model and gives the representative's existing notes the fence they lack. The outcome history this solution keeps is what the subconscious's intuition draws on (remember-and-recall:outcome_precedents). A quest can have several representatives (owner's direction, 2026-10-28): each keeps its own view across its own assigned quests, a request reads only the view of the representative chosen to handle it (select-a-rep), and facts every representative on the quest needs, such as a decline or the quest's own state, are kept at the quest level so all of them see them.
measures_of_success: A decline holds across later requests under the same intent and its descendants; a correction is applied where it bears; chat and background work agree; a request in a child quest starts from its ancestors' views; no item reaches a sibling intent or another person; nothing adds time before the reply. When several representatives share a quest, a decline made with one holds for all of them. Standing conditions: Fence by the intent hierarchy on every read and write. Keep the person's own words verbatim. Never create or link an intent without the person.
parameters: The implementation, how many ancestor levels a request reads, the size of each view, when views are refreshed, and the model tier for any summary.
inputs: The representative, its assigned quests and their roles from the host, the host's intent hierarchy and quest placements, each finished request's outcome, and the stores' records.
outputs: For a request the representative handles: its standing view across its assigned quests and the views of their ancestor intents, with the source of each item, fenced to those quests and ancestors.
effects: Writes the maintained view in the background after a request; no work before the reply.
usage_notes: Selected today: separate_stores. The proposal is per_rep_assigned_view; per_quest_note is the narrow case and per_intent_cascade the view without representatives.

name: Critical thinking: the enforcer of ESOI metrics on every request
description: Holds every request the system serves (a chat turn, a queued task, a deep run) to the specification's relevant metric by code: it finds the slice, has the metric read before and after, and answers a regression or a missing metric instead of only displaying it, so the specification is applied everywhere rather than where the work is largest.
purpose: Makes sure everything the system does applies the relevant ESOI metric and leaves it improved, or at least not worse.
approach: Finds the relevant slice of the specification for each request, measures its authoritative metric before and after by code, and holds the result to improve or not regress, proposing a metric where none exists.
out_of_scope: Finding the slice and reading a metric (the specification slice, meters and ledger do that), writing a run's changes back onto the records, and choosing which metric a solution should have, which is the owner's to confirm.
milestones: 1. A replayed set of requests across chat turns, queued tasks and deep runs exists, each labelled with the metric it should be held to or none, and deep_runs_only and instruction_only have recorded results on it. 2. every_request_measured holds every request whose labelled metric can be read, with no time added before the reply. 3. measured_proposed_and_answered leaves no regression and no missing metric without a response, and proposes a metric for the metric-less requests.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm. The specification owner's definition (2026-10-28): an enforcer of the effective application of ESOI on every request, making sure the relevant metrics are applied and improving on everything the system does; a person's quest metrics and experiments are one case of it, not its definition. The owner's standing principle: a rule for AI is built into the flow and enforced by code, never left to an instruction. Built and settled 2026-10-22, by direction rather than a measured win: around every deep goal the slice is found without a model (core/spec_slice.py), the metric is read before and after by the runner's own meters (core/metric_meter.py), rows go to a ledger and are reconciled (core/metric_results.py), and a changed run with nothing on record is asked once and otherwise marked missing (core/goal_metrics.py); the rows are shown in the terminal and the host's chat. Missing, read in the code on 2026-10-28: the goal metrics are created only in the deep run (core/orchestrator_deep_run.py), so chat turns and in-process work take no reading; a slice exists only when a repository's records are found and the selection is confident, and a quest's own specification reaches chat through the intent frame, not a slice; when the reading after is worse, nothing acts; a missing metric is shown and not followed up. Open recommendation, not decided: keep this as the enforcing role that uses iterate-by-spec and the metric modules as mechanisms, rather than widening iterate-by-spec, because its unit is every request and its best is coverage and no regression, while iterate-by-spec is defined per deep goal and judged by first-pass acceptance; if its only arm turns out to be iterate-by-spec applied everywhere, the two should merge.
measures_of_success: Every request whose metric can be read is measured before and after by code; none is left worse without a response; a request with no metric gets one proposed; for a person's quest, an uncertain choice leads to a proposed experiment. Standing conditions: Decide from the ledger and the runner's own records, never from a model's words. Never invent a reading. Add no time before a chat reply.
parameters: Which kinds of request are held (chat, task, deep), which meter reads a chat turn and when, what counts as a regression, the response to one (retry, revert, follow-up, escalation), and whether a metric is proposed when none applies.
inputs: The request, its slice of the specification or the quest's own specification, the ledger and the runner's records of what changed.
outputs: Per request: the metric applied with its reading before and after, or the reason none applies, or a proposed metric; and for a regression or a missing metric, the response taken.
effects: Reads metrics through the meters, after a chat reply in the background; writes ledger rows; may open a follow-up task or a proposal; never edits the owner's records without consent.
usage_notes: Selected today: deep_runs_only. instruction_only is the floor that shows what code enforcement adds.

name: Justified model calls
description: Keeps every model call tied to a registered prompt spec with an owner solution and metric, so a call stays only while its measured value outweighs its cost and time.
purpose: Gives an operator a known value, cost and time for every model call, so spend and latency go only to prompts that earn them and a cheaper or faster option is not missed.
approach: Every prompt is a registered PromptSpec (id, owner solution, metric, tier, cache layer, output schema, no-em-dash rule) in core/prompt_specs.py. One enforced call path, checked by tests/test_prompt_specs.py with a shrinking baseline, admits only registered prompts. A per-call ablation drops or downgrades the call and checks the owner metric.
out_of_scope: Choosing the model tier for a turn (choose-a-model-tier), the daily budget (track-usage-and-cost), and the content of any one prompt.
milestones: 1. Every call site is a registered spec and the baseline of unregistered sites is empty. 2. Each spec has a per-call ablation row on production-shaped cases. 3. Each spec has a budget for cost, tokens and latency set from the value its owner metric shows.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: dictated by Joshua 2026-10-28 and recorded as given, to be confirmed by him; not built beyond the registry and the enforcement test, so the metric is unmeasured. Known today: the call sites still unregistered are listed in tests/prompt_spec_baseline.txt; spend-weighted value not computed.
measures_of_success: The metric is read from recorded rows without invented readings. Standing conditions: Never invent a reading. Label rows taken from eval traces until production data exists.
parameters: The bar (0.8) and each prompt's own budget for cost, tokens and latency.
inputs: The per-call usage records tagged with the spec id (quest_ai_runner/usage.py) and production-shaped eval cases (quest_ai_prod_examples shapes).
outputs: A per-prompt table and the share of average model spend that is justified.
effects: No model call of its own except the ablation runs, which are paid and run only by decision with a budget.
usage_notes: Selected today: spec_registry. The ablation arm is proposed and not built.
